policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'the angel of the church in Ephesus' renders the genitive article as 'of the'; the dative alternative would not account for that relation.
ASV repeats the possessive in 'thy toil' after 'thy works,' supporting the added σου after κόπον.
ASV 'call themselves apostles' can render the predicate construction either with or without explicit εἶναι.
ASV 'hast not grown weary' preserves the perfect sense of οὐ κεκοπίακες rather than the aorist alternative.
The two readings are spelling variants of the same perfect form, both rendered by ASV 'art fallen.'
ASV 'I come to thee' has no 'quickly' here, excluding the RP addition ταχύ.
ASV has 'the Paradise of God,' not 'of my God,' excluding the addition μου.
ASV 'the angel of the church in Smyrna' renders the genitive article as 'of the'; the dative alternative would not account for that relation.
ASV begins the object of 'I know' with 'thy tribulation' and has no preceding 'thy works and,' excluding the RP addition.
ASV 'Fear not the things which thou art about to suffer' reflects μὴ negating 'fear'; μηδὲν would instead supply an object meaning 'nothing.'
ASV 'art about to suffer' does not distinguish the present infinitive πάσχειν from aorist παθεῖν.
ASV has the simple interjection 'behold' and no additional emphatic expression corresponding to δή.
ASV 'is about to cast' does not distinguish the present infinitive βάλλειν from aorist βαλεῖν.
ASV's predictive 'ye shall have tribulation' supports indicative ἕξετε rather than subjunctive ἔχητε.
ASV proceeds directly from 'I know' to 'where thou dwellest' and has no 'thy works and,' excluding the RP addition.
ASV explicitly coordinates 'and thou holdest fast my name,' retaining καί.
ASV has 'even in the days of Antipas' without an added relative phrase 'in which,' excluding ἐν αἷς.
ASV 'my faithful one' explicitly represents μου, excluding its omission.
ASV 'who taught Balak' reflects the aorist active ἐδίδαξεν with Balak as direct object, rather than imperfect ἐδίδασκεν with a dative.
ASV has no conjunction before 'to eat things sacrificed to idols'; its 'and' occurs only before 'to commit fornication.'
ASV 'the teaching of the Nicolaitans' explicitly represents the added genitive article τῶν as 'the.'
ASV 'give of the hidden manna' has no infinitive 'to eat,' excluding the RP addition φαγεῖν.
ASV 'the angel of the church in Thyatira' renders the genitive article as 'of the'; the dative alternative would not account for that relation.
ASV preserves the base order exactly in 'thy love and faith'; the alternative reverses the two nouns.
ASV 'the woman Jezebel' has no possessive 'thy,' excluding the addition σοῦ.
ASV's relative clause 'who calleth herself a prophetess' reflects participial λέγουσα rather than finite λέγει.
ASV 'except they repent' requires the subjunctive μετανοήσωσιν rather than future indicative μετανοήσουσιν.
ASV present passive 'are broken to shivers' supports συντρίβεται rather than future συντριβήσεται.
